title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 119 (Inspection of minute-books of general meeting)

content.overview: The minute-books of general meetings and postal-ballot resolutions must be kept at the registered office and open to any Member's inspection during business hours without charge, subject to reasonable restrictions that allow at least two hours each business day. A Member may obtain a copy within seven working days on payment of the prescribed fee. Refusal or delay attracts separate company/officer penalties, and the Tribunal may order immediate inspection or supply of the copy.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 119 (Inspection of minute-books of general meeting). Minute-books of general meetings and resolutions passed by postal ballot must be kept at the registered office and be open during business hours to any Member without charge. Reasonable restrictions may be imposed by the articles or in general meeting, but at least two hours in each business day must be allowed for inspection. A Member is entitled to a copy within seven working days after requesting it and paying the prescribed fee. If inspection is refused or the copy is not furnished within the specified time, the company is liable to a penalty of ₹25,000 and every officer in default to ₹5,000 for each refusal or default. Without prejudice to those penalties, the Tribunal may order immediate inspection or direct that the requested copy be sent forthwith. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Location and inspection
sections.body: Books containing minutes of general meetings or resolutions passed by postal ballot must be kept at the registered office and be open during business hours to any Member without charge. Reasonable restrictions may be imposed by the articles or in general meeting, but at least two hours in each business day must be allowed for inspection.

sections.heading: Copies
sections.body: A Member is entitled to be furnished with a copy of the relevant minutes within seven working days after making a request to the company and paying the prescribed fee.

sections.heading: Penalty for refusal or delay
sections.body: If inspection is refused or a requested copy is not furnished within the specified time, the company is liable to a penalty of ₹25,000 and every officer in default is liable to a penalty of ₹5,000 for each refusal or default.

sections.heading: Tribunal direction
sections.body: Without prejudice to action under subsection (3), the Tribunal may direct immediate inspection of the minute-books or order that the requested copy be sent forthwith.

examples.title: Inspection access
examples.body: A company may impose reasonable restrictions, but it must still allow at least two hours on each business day for Member inspection of the covered minute-books.

examples.title: Delayed copy request
examples.body: If a Member has requested a copy and paid the prescribed fee, check whether the company furnished it within seven working days; if not, consider the statutory penalty and Tribunal direction provisions.

hypotheticals.question: A company allows Member inspection for only one hour each business day, citing reasonable restrictions in its articles. Is that consistent with section 119(1)?
hypotheticals.analysis: The section permits reasonable restrictions but expressly requires at least two hours in each business day to be allowed for inspection. The stated one-hour period does not meet that minimum.

hypotheticals.question: A company does not furnish requested minutes within seven working days after a Member's request and payment of the prescribed fee. What does section 119 provide?
hypotheticals.analysis: Subsection (3) provides a penalty of ₹25,000 for the company and ₹5,000 for each officer in default for each refusal or default. Under subsection (4), the Tribunal may also order immediate inspection or direct that the copy be sent forthwith.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming reasonable restrictions can reduce inspection time below two hours in each business day.
misconceptions.correction: The section expressly requires at least two hours each business day for inspection.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the copy deadline as seven calendar days.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (2) states seven working days after the request, on payment of the prescribed fee.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the penalties and Tribunal remedy for refusal or delay.
misconceptions.correction: Subsections (3) and (4) provide separate penalties and a Tribunal power to order immediate inspection or delivery of the copy.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What inspection rights does section 119 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Members may inspect general-meeting minute-books at the registered office during business hours and obtain copies on payment of the prescribed fee within seven days. The NCLT may order relief on unlawful refusal.

examTips: State the scope: general-meeting minutes, not Board minutes.
Mention copy fees, seven-day period and the NCLT remedy.
revisionPoints: Registered office; Member inspection free during business hours; at least two hours each business day.
Copy within seven working days on payment of prescribed fee.
Company penalty ₹25,000 and officer-in-default penalty ₹5,000 per refusal/default.
Tribunal may order immediate inspection or supply of the copy.
